title: Youth justice service days: the fall traced to one program's count
question: The youth department's Justice Services days fell from 194,889 to 36,382 in a year. Which strategy and which grantee account for it?
finding: Justice Services participant service days went from 194,889 in 2024-25 to 36,382 in 2025-26. School Crisis Support alone went from 166,096 to 4,508, and one program in it — Community Youth Center of San Francisco, School Violence Interrupters — reported 163,663 days in 2024-25 (84% of the whole service area) and 943 in 2025-26. Its page shows no participant count, 126 service dates, 26 school incidents and 53 supports in 2024-25: about 1,299 participant days per service date. Without that program, the service area's days rose from 31,226 to 35,439 (+13%).
how: Read from the department's printed year-end pages: the Justice Services service-area page, the eight strategy pages and every program page saved, for both years (the heading on each page gives the year; the script checks it against the file name). The eight strategy pages' participant service days add up exactly to the service-area figure in both years (checked on every run). Incident and support counts are the sums of the school-crisis tables on the program page.
limits: A participant service day is the department's count of days of participation, including young people reported only in aggregate (its own footnote). A school-violence program that counts every student reached at a campus event in aggregate would produce a large number honestly; the page gives no method. The 2025-26 figure may be the corrected one, or the counting rule may have changed between years; either way the fall in the service area's days is a counting question, not evidence that services were cut. Nothing here says the grant was paid by the day.
